name: Siaha
overview: Siaha was a male member of the tribe of Levi who served as a temple servant. His role placed him within the Levitical duties connected to the service of the temple, as recorded in Ezra 2:44. Beyond this, Scripture provides no additional personal details about him.
namesAndTitles: The name Siaha, appearing in Ezra 2:44, means 'assembly' in Hebrew. A variant of his name, Sia, also meaning 'assembly,' is found in Nehemiah 7:47. These names reflect a connection to the community or congregation, consistent with his Levitical service.
familyAndRelationships: Siaha is identified as a descendant of Levi, indicating his Levitical lineage. Scripture does not record any further family relationships beyond this tribal affiliation and his role as a temple servant.
scriptureSignificance: Siaha's significance lies in his role as a temple servant from the tribe of Levi during the post-exilic period. His mention in Ezra 2:44 highlights the restoration of temple worship and the reestablishment of Levitical duties after the return from Babylonian exile. Through individuals like Siaha, the continuity of God's ordained temple service was maintained, underscoring the faithfulness of God's people in preserving worship practices.
